subject: Reservation flex buffer proposal — DynaRetail pilot / autoscale exception
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ops@dyna-retail.com
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reservation flex buffer proposal — DynaRetail pilot / autoscale exception

Team —

High level: DynaRetail is ready to spin up a 12-week enterprise pilot starting mid-June. They expect sustained low-latency traffic during peak merchandising windows with short high-throughput spikes for batch re-ranks (30–90s). They asked for a 40% dedicated buffer on top of our normal pool reservation to guarantee throughput during peak windows.

Why I'm asking: this is a strategic pilot (HS-8342) and their procurement wants a one-line commitment for a temporary reservation lane. Product is asking for predictable latency, infra wants safe fallbacks, and finance needs a cost delta for contracting.

Proposal (initial):
- Reserve 25% extra GPU capacity for 8 weeks (pilot period) in their us-west region pool
- Allow autoscale-policy TTL override during the pilot (disable preemption for reserved slice for scheduled peak windows only)
- Reconcile costs at the end of pilot; if usage < 30% of buffer we rollback early and bill prorated compensation

Tradeoffs we need to call out:
- Larger buffer (40%) reduces risk but materially increases monthly unit cost; small buffer risks elevated request queuing during spikes
- Warm-up / KV-cache priming is necessary to hit latency SLOs quickly — that will add scheduled run costs

Asks:
1) Marcus/David — can you provide capacity feasibility and a rough cost delta (backend calc attached: reserve-calcs.xlsx)?
2) Laura — product sign-off on acceptable buffer level vs. impact to fidelity and rollout timeline
3) Finance/Contracts (Aditya cc'd) — quick call on billing model (fixed monthly buffer vs. usage-based top-ups)

Attachments: reserve-calcs.xlsx (spreadsheet with rough unit math), pilot-MAP-v1.pdf (customer MAP & timeline)

If we can agree today on the buffer and TTL, I can send a single-line approval to DynaRetail procurement and bake this into the pilot MOU.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ops@dyna-retail.com
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation flex buffer proposal — DynaRetail pilot / autoscale exception

Kim — thanks for the summary and the calc. A few clarifying points from infra: 

1) What does "disable preemption for reserved slice" mean operationally? We can mark the slice as non-preemptible for scheduled windows (e.g., 06:00–10:00 PT daily during the pilot) but fully disabling preemption cluster-wide is risky. Suggest scoped windows and a hard rollback trigger.

2) Regarding sizing: 25% of the pool feels reasonable for an 8-week pilot if traffic shape is bursty but predictable. 40% is definitely heavy — if we go that route we should scope it to daytime windows only, not 24/7.

3) KV-cache priming: we should add a scheduled warm-up job (see warmup-runbook.md attached by Laura later). That will reduce the cold-latency tail but requires a small batch runner and short model loads.

Quick feasibility ask for David: can you run a slot-level simulation for the following windows (simulate today if possible):
- baseline steady traffic: 120 qps sustained
- spikes: 250 qps for 90s every 3 hours (estimated)
Return: expected queue depth with 0%, 20%, 25%, 40% buffers. Also include estimated risk of preemption if we don't alter autoscale TTLs.

Cc'd Aditya for contract/billing POV — Marcus will need approval on TTL/timeboxed preemption exemptions.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ops@dyna-retail.com, contracts@dyna-retail.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation flex buffer proposal — DynaRetail pilot / autoscale exception

Appreciate the context. Product perspective: we need DynaRetail to hit a P95 generation latency <= 180ms for interactive features and < 300ms for batch re-ranks under peak. That implies we must avoid cold starts during peak windows — so warm-up is non-negotiable.

Proposed compromise:
- Approve a 25% buffer for the 8-week pilot with the following constraints:
  * The 25% buffer applies during scheduled peak windows only (2x/day 4-hour windows)
  * Outside scheduled windows, buffer can be elastically sized down by autoscaler to reclaim capacity for other customers
  * We require two warm-up waves 30 minutes and 5 minutes before each peak window to populate KV caches and JIT kernels

This reduces cost vs. 40% while satisfying latency needs. If infra sim shows queue risk still high at 25% then we can increase to 30% for the first two weeks and then revert.

Can finance provide a quick delta estimate for this pattern (timeboxed windowed buffer vs. full-time buffer)? If we bill DynaRetail a premium for scheduled reserved windows it keeps our economics intact.

Attachment: warmup-runbook.md (I will upload to Notion; pasted key steps in the linked doc)

-Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ops@dyna-retail.com, contracts@dyna-retail.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation flex buffer proposal — DynaRetail pilot / autoscale exception

Folks — I ran the slot sims Marcus requested (attached spreadsheet cells summarized). TL;DR: 8-week, 25% timeboxed buffer (two 4-hour windows/day) is feasible and keeps P95 latency within targets with warm-up waves. Expected net cost delta to customer: ~+22% for pilot months compared to a pure usage model; to Redwood (opportunity cost) the reclaimable hours outside windows recover ~40% of the reserved capacity cost.

Operational guardrails I recommend: 
- Authorize a temporary autoscale TTL override limited to scheduled windows (max 10 weeks; must sign-off by product + finance for any extension)
- Implement an automated rollback trigger: if average buffer utilization < 12% for three consecutive days, the system will reduce buffer by half and notify stakeholders
- Pre-flight: schedule two warm-up waves and a dry-run 48 hours before production start to validate KV priming and kernel cache behavior

Procurement note for Aditya: bill as a scheduled-reservation add-on tied to HS-8342; propose splitting the buffer premium 70/30 (70% billed fixed to DynaRetail; 30% absorbed as platform promo credit for pilot). We can adjust after pilot based on utilization.

I approve moving forward with the 25% timeboxed buffer under the guardrails above. Marcus, please publish the runbook steps (warmup + TTL configuration) and ops playbook. Laura, please confirm you will accept the 25% windowed buffer in writing so I can add the change to the capacity control plane.

Thanks — quick thumbs from Aditya would be great and then Kim if you want to send the MOU note to DynaRetail procurement I think we can close.

-David
David Kim
Director, Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference
